correctness.rationale: At fixed \(S\), Gini ordering is by \(D(x)=\sum_{i<j}(x_j-x_i)\), while Palma is the exact rational \(x_{10}/(x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4)\). Exhaustive exact comparison of all positive ten-part partitions proves zero strict reversals through \(S=16\) and exactly two at \(S=17\).

value.rationale: Gini and Palma are policy-relevant inequality summaries with deliberately different sensitivity. Ten households is the smallest exact decile representation, and fixing total removes scale. The theorem gives a natural minimum-resolution benchmark for opposite strict judgments and classifies its complete first layer.
